title: Neapolitan Pizza

ingredients.title: For the Dough
items: 600 g “00” flour (finely milled Italian flour; Caputo is ideal)
2 g fresh yeast (or 1 g active dry yeast)

ingredients.title: For the Sauce
items: 400 g San Marzano DOP tomatoes (whole, peeled)

ingredients.title: For the Topping (per pizza)
items: 80–100 g fresh mozzarella di bufala (buffalo mozzarella), drained and torn into pieces
1–2 tsp extra virgin olive oil (for drizzling)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Dough Preparation
steps: In a large bowl, dissolve yeast in the water.
Gradually add flour, mixing gently by hand or with a dough scraper.
Once half the flour is incorporated, add the salt. Continue mixing until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead on a clean surface for 10–15 minutes until smooth, elastic, and slightly tacky (or use a stand mixer on low speed for ~8 minutes).
Cover and let rest at room temperature for 2 hours.
Divide dough into 4 balls (~250 g each), shape tightly, and place in a proofing box or lightly floured tray.
Cover and ferment at room temperature for 8–12 hours (or cold ferment in the fridge for 24 hours for deeper flavor).

instruction.title: Step 2 – Tomato Sauce
steps: Crush San Marzano tomatoes by hand or with a food mill.
Stir in olive oil, salt, and torn basil.
Do not overcook or puree smooth—texture is key.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Shaping
steps: Preheat oven with a pizza stone/steel to its maximum temperature (ideally 450–500°C in a wood-fired oven, or 280–300°C in a home oven with steel).
On a floured surface, gently press one dough ball from the center outward, leaving a 2–3 cm rim for the cornicione (crust).
Stretch to ~25–28 cm (10–11 inches) without using a rolling pin.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Assembly
steps: Spread 2–3 tbsp of tomato sauce over the base.
Place fresh basil leaves and drizzle lightly with olive oil.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Baking
steps: Wood-fired oven: Bake for 60–90 seconds at ~450–500°C until the crust is leopard-spotted, puffy, and slightly charred.
Home oven with stone/steel: Bake for 5–7 minutes at maximum heat, finishing with a quick broil if needed for blistering.

chefTips: The hallmark of Pizza Napoletana is the airy cornicione (puffed crust) with leopard spotting.
Keep toppings minimal—simplicity is key to balance.
Always use high-quality ingredients (Caputo “00” flour, San Marzano tomatoes, buffalo mozzarella, extra virgin olive oil).
